_readme: Machine-readable source registry. Design + reasoning: scripts/data-sources.md. Tier A may be ingested by collectors; Tier B may only be cited in a model's sources[] and MUST NOT back a ladder; Tier C is vendor-primary. Each entry lists the hosts that identify it, so any URL in the data resolves to a tier and a licence; validate-data.mjs enforces the tier rules; collect-epoch.mjs reads the epoch-ai entry. Endpoints below were each fetched and confirmed live on 2026-07-25 — nothing here is aspirational.

sources.name: Epoch AI Benchmarking Hub
sources.attribution: Epoch AI, 'AI Benchmarking Hub'. Published online at epoch.ai. Retrieved from https://epoch.ai/benchmarks/use-this-data
gives: independently-run benchmark scores with stderr (gpqa_diamond, swe_bench_verified, math_level_5, frontiermath, simpleqa_verified)
mirrored external leaderboards under their own licences
sources.conflicts: Epoch mirrors CursorBench rather than re-running it, and CursorBench is published by Cursor, which ships its own coding model. Separately, OpenAI funded Epoch's FrontierMath benchmark with dataset access, disclosed only after the fact.
sources.notes: Derived files carry their origin licence: aider_polyglot_external and terminalbench_external are Apache-2.0, not CC-BY. Anything ingested from those must credit the original leaderboard.

sources.name: Terminal-Bench 2.x
gives: cross-lab agentic scores with average cost per task in USD
sources.conflicts: None known. Independent and audited, with public trajectories.
sources.notes: No per-model reasoning-effort rungs, so it cannot back an effort ladder — it is a candidate for a separate panel. tbench.ai/leaderboard 301-redirects; use the Hugging Face dataset as the machine endpoint.

sources.name: OpenRouter models API
sources.attribution: Pricing and model IDs via OpenRouter
gives: model IDs at or near launch (the launch-detector signal)
sources.conflicts: Provider pass-through pricing, NOT vendor list price — it may legitimately differ from the official page.
sources.notes: Never write an OpenRouter price into models.json. It is a drift alarm and a new-model detector only; list prices come from the vendor's own pricing page.

sources.name: Artificial Analysis
gives: Intelligence Index vs cost per task, with separate per-effort entries
sources.conflicts: Runs paid pre-release evaluations with the labs, including for Claude Opus 5 itself.
sources.notes: RULED OUT as a feed, 2026-07-25: the free tier is internal-use-only and a public site counts as redistribution, which needs a Commercial licence at an unpublished price. Decision: paid licences are ruled out. Do not reopen and do not request a quote. Citing a figure in sources[] with a link is fine; ingesting is not.

sources.name: llm-stats.com
gives: broad model coverage, useful for discovery only
sources.conflicts: Aggregator — thinner provenance than whoever ran the eval.
sources.notes: Use to notice that a number exists somewhere, then go to the primary source for it.

sources.name: LMArena
sources.conflicts: Preference, not correctness. No cost axis and no effort rungs.
sources.notes: Already used as its own separate signal in usage.lenses. Keep it there.

sources.name: Vals AI
gives: independent domain evals reporting accuracy, cost and latency
sources.conflicts: Sells private evaluation infrastructure to the labs — same conflict class as Artificial Analysis.
sources.notes: One effort setting per run, so it cannot back a ladder. Watch, don't ingest.

sources.name: Vendor pricing pages, model cards and launch posts
sources.conflicts: The most conflicted source class — a lab grading its own model. Fastest at launch, which is why it is allowed at all.
sources.notes: Always label source_kind 'vendor-reported'. Never the only source once a Tier-A number exists for the same field. List price is the one field where a vendor page outranks everything.
